summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby specialized in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, he taught at McGill and Yale before holding professorships at Trinity College, Toronto, and the University of Toronto from 1971 to 1999.

Willard L. Johnson was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Oberlin College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he taught at CSU Long Beach, San Diego State University, Del Mar College, and Oberlin College.

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at Oberlin and Harvard under Alfred North Whitehead, and with Rudolf Carnap, he spent his career primarily at Harvard University from 1933 to 1978, alongside visiting posts at Oxford and Wesleyan.

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and at the University of Hamburg. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and taught at Heidelberg University from around 1970 to 1993.

Willem Caland was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. After Stedelijk Gymnasium Breda, he served as Lektor and Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1903–1930).

Willem Frederik Stutterheim was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Utrecht University and completed his Ph.D. at Leiden under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, later directing the Oudheidkundige Dienst, Surakarta College (1926–1936), and Dinas Purbakala (1937).

Willem Lodewijk van Helten was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University, where he studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He taught at Gymnasium Erasmianum before serving as professor at the University of Groningen from 1882 to 1911.

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (circa 1970–1983) and held academic posts at Leiden University (circa 1983–2017) and the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held posts at the University of Virginia, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

William Abbott Oldfather was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Hanover College, Harvard University, and the University of Munich. He held faculty posts at Northwestern University (1903–1909) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1909–1945).

William Austin Montriou was an Indologist and legal scholar. He served as an advocate at the Calcutta High Court and held an appointment as Professor of Law and Jurisprudence at Presidency University.
William Blackstone was educated at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford. He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from approximately 1758 to 1766.

William Bright was a linguist and Indologist who studied at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Deccan College, the U.S. Department of State, UC Berkeley, UCLA (1959–1988), and the University of Colorado Boulder (1988–2006).

William C. Kirby is a historian and sinologist educated at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He held professorial and administrative posts at Washington University in St. Louis (1980–1992) and Harvard University, including Dean and Fairbank Center Director.

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He served as Professor of Sanscrit at Fort William College (1801–1830) and as Principal of Serampore College (1818–1832), which he co-founded.

William Carlson Smith was a scholar of Indology who studied at Grand Island College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Southern California. Between 1912 and 1915, he conducted educational work for the American Baptist Missionary Union.

William Chambers was an Indologist who served as a political servant for the East India Company (~1765–1793). He was an interpreter at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1775–1792) and a member of The Asiatic Society.
William Charles Macready was an Indologist who studied at Christ Church and the East India Company College. In 1854, he served in the Ceylon Civil Service as an Assistant Government Agent.

William Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, SUNY, and Stony Brook University as a Distinguished Professor.

William Doderet was an Indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1880. He later served as the University Teacher of Marathi at the University of Cambridge from 1910 to 1919.
